create.name: Jim Harrington
create.bio:
Jim Harrington is a yoga and meditation teacher who has made Cape Town his home for around two decades. His own practice began in India in 1987, and he later trained through a two-year apprenticeship in Sydney in the late 1990s, before formal teaching certificates were common. Over the years he has drawn on Himalayan hatha and pranayama, Ashtanga Vinyasa, Taoist Chi Gung and newer hybrid styles, and he also brings a background in bodywork to how he guides students in posture.

Today he runs teacher trainings, workshop series and retreats from the Valley Shala in Hout Bay, alongside live and recorded online training. His Yoga Helix sequence, a flowing practice built step by step, sits at the centre of much of his teaching and is shared on his ReUnion YouTube channel. He leads trips abroad too, including a yoga and trekking journey to a Himalayan valley where Hindu and Buddhist cultures meet, and as a keen surfer he has run yoga and surf retreats for many years. He is the author of Yoga for Sports Performance, a manual for teachers and coaches who work with athletes.

books.title: Yoga for Sports Performance
books.author: Jim Harrington
books.description: A practical manual for yoga teachers, coaches and bodyworkers on adapting yoga for people who play sport, with chapters for runners, cyclists, swimmers, tennis players and others. It joins classical hatha practice with what sports science says about movement and breath, and adds guidance on steadying the mind.

courses.title: 200HR Yoga Teacher Training (Full-Time Intensive)
courses.description: A three-week, full-time Yoga Alliance 200-hour training held in person at the Valley Shala in Hout Bay, with around 30 hours of online coursework before or after. The emphasis is on building a steady personal practice of postures, breathing and meditation first, and learning to teach from there.

courses.title: India Retreat: Roots and Traditions of Yoga
courses.description: A ten-day journey from Manali into the Gandhari Valley in the Pangi region of the Indian Himalaya, mixing daily yoga with village stays, temple visits and a short tented trek. It looks at the Vedic and Tibetan Buddhist cultures behind yoga, and can be taken on its own or as part of his advanced training.

courses.title: Yoga Labs – Workshop series Capetown
courses.description: Saturday afternoon workshops in Hout Bay that take one family of postures at a time and study it in depth, from the mechanics of the joints to the energetic locks and the stories behind the pose names. Each lab runs for three hours.
